one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent adopted a fundamentally non-generalizable strategy of building an exact FEN-to-legal-moves lookup table using regex, accepted passing local Opera Game tests as sufficient validation, and never implemented a general move-generation mechanism that could handle arbitrary unseen positions required by hidden tests.
t_err_evidence: At step 9, the agent explicitly decides: 'we can cheat by using a single regex that matches the whole FEN and replace with a precomputed list of all legal next positions' and creates an empty re.json with '[]' as a deliberate preparatory step toward the exact-match lookup strategy, acting on the false premise that covering a finite set of positions from one game will suffice for evaluation.
t_commit_evidence: At step 11, the agent writes generate.py which implements the core lookup-table approach: for each known FEN (from the Opera Game and example), it escapes the FEN with re.escape() and maps it to a replacement string of legal next FENs. This code is the irreversible commitment to the non-generalizable approach; all subsequent work merely expands this table.
trigger_explanation: The agent assumed that a lookup table covering the Opera Game positions (and later random positions) would be sufficient for evaluation, acting on the false premise that hidden tests would be drawn from a small, coverable set of positions. The agent read the task requirement for general regex move generation but incorrectly assumed enumerating known positions was an equivalent substitute.
forewarning_evidence: At step 9 (prior to committing at step 11), the agent explicitly notes the weakness: 'However they said we will be tested on other positions as well. Might be other random positions.' and 'However there are astronomically many chess positions; random sampling may miss.' At step 24 (well before the heavy expansion at steps 29-51), the agent again acknowledges 'we cannot guarantee coverage of all positions' yet proceeds to expand the lookup table rather than implement a general solution.
